National Assembly
Upper House
Twenty-ninth Session
Complete Proceedings
Proceedings
14 Magh
2082
Wednesday
Meeting
Number - 4
The meeting of the National Assembly commenced today at 13:21 hours under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members,
(13:21 hours)
The proceedings commence. Names of Honourable Members have been received to speak during the Zero Hour. I will provide time to the Honourable Members to speak. I have allocated 1 minute to each Honourable Member to speak during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Kamala Pant.
Honourable Mr. Kamala Pant
(Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, Sir,
(13:22 hours)
Sometimes there are natural disasters, sometimes man-made disasters, and we have experienced many natural disasters in our generation as well. A major program was also held in remembrance of the 1990 earthquake. The state also observed that day of remembrance, but the earthquake victims of 2072 BS received some relief, and apart from some minor issues, the earthquake victims received all the cooperation that the government had pledged. But why have the Jajarkot earthquake victims been so insulted? Are they not citizens? Do the people there not need relief? The government promised, so many days have passed... (Time expired).
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Narayan Dutt Mishra.
(13:23 hours)
Honourable Mr. Narayan Dutt Mishra (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, Sir,
(13:23 hours)
It's surprising! The north-south roads in Kailali district, which we worked hard to build and which connect the highway to the Hulaaki Road, are in such a bad state that it is easier to drive on gravel or dirt roads, but when driving on these roads, people of our age feel like their backs will break. Therefore, drawing the government's attention to the repair, maintenance, and widening of these neglected roads, the Sahajpur-Boktan-Dipayal road in Doti district seems to be in limbo. We request that prompt action be taken to blacktop this road. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar.
(13:24 hours)
Honourable Mr. Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):-
(13:24 hours)
Honourable Chairperson, Sir, in the fiscal year 2081/082, the Ministry of Finance had allocated 30 crore rupees for the upliftment and progress of the Dalit community. That amount has been... In this fiscal year, 40 crore has been allocated. What is the status of its implementation? The Ministry of Industry has not provided information on this, and I am expressing my concern. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Madan Kumar Shah "Garima".
(13:24 hours)
Honourable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party, Unified Socialist):
(13:25 hours)
Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the country is in an election mood. New methods and mediums of election campaigning are being used, including social media like Facebook, TikTok, and even AI. There is a possibility of misinformation among voters. I appeal and request the voters that not all content and information on social media is true. Understand it only after verifying. I want to draw the serious attention of the government, through you, Mr. Chairperson, to bring individuals and platforms that spread false and misleading content under the purview of the law and to make the elections safe, fair, and secure. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma.
(13:26 hours)
Honourable Mr. Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, Sir,
(13:26 hours)
There is a Zero Hour. The situation is also zero. Subtracting or adding zero from zero results in zero. When speaking during Zero Hour, first, it seems necessary to transform this zero into a dynamic force, or for a democratic party, or for national unity. I want to compare the Honourable Ministers who have broken all their commitments and are running away after making money, joining the same party, with the tendency of rats fleeing when a ship sinks. When the Honourable Prime Minister did not make his assets public, none of the contenders for the Prime Minister's post during the elections seemed to have done so. Therefore, Manmohanji, Sushilji, today, senior leader Krishnaji, have those who destroyed the country by setting fire to Lachha Garh returned to deceive us again? Honourable Chairperson, Sir, are they not walking around with their heads held high? Caution is necessary, we must keep an eye out, lest tomorrow the national animal, Pashupatinath Temple, women's dignity, and the poor and helpless are attacked again. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.
(13:27 hours)
Honourable Mr. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepal Communist Party, Unified Socialist):
(13:27 hours)
Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the road from Palpa to Rampur was built with many vehicles. Now, after the Kaligandaki Corridor was built, the management of that road has caused great inconvenience to the travellers going to Mathagadhi and the farmers there. The dust, the slopes, the cardamom, the road going to Rampur, and nowadays the road to Rampur... has become extremely dilapidated. I want to monitor that. And the second thing is this... (Time expired).
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.
(13:28 hours)
Honourable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):-
(13:29 hours)
Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the movement of Bhadra 23 and 24 was completely unbelievable, extraordinary, and novel in the history of Nepal. The movement on Bhadra 23 was called by the Janajati people with rightful demands. It was praiseworthy. However, during that movement, the then government brutally suppressed it peacefully and killed many people. That is condemnable. I want to condemn it. Who is the controller of the movement on the 24th, which involved criminal activities and destructive acts? The Janajati people do not take responsibility for it. So, who is it? We did not do such activities even during the great ten-year People's War. Although it was our strong struggle, it was carried out. Therefore, I want to state that a thorough investigation into the criminal activities of the movement on the 24th is necessary. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Sonam Geljen Sherpa.
(13:30 hours)
Honourable Mr. Sonam Geljen Sherpa (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honourable
(13:30 hours)
Chairperson, Sir, the Election Commission and the government have announced elections, and the elections are to be held on Falgun 21st. However, in the Himalayan region, people who have descended to the lower regions due to the cold on Falgun 21st, the people there, are not in a position to go there. Now, it is estimated that only about 30 to 40 percent of the votes in the Himalayan region will be cast. Therefore, there is a possibility that 60 percent of the voters will be disenfranchised. I draw the government's attention to this. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members, the Zero Hour concludes with the Honourable Members speaking. Honourable Members, names of members have been received on a party basis to speak during the Special Time. Now I will provide time to the Honourable Members to speak. First, Honourable Member Maya Prasad Sharma. Time: 12 minutes. After this, Honourable Member Narayan Dutt Bhat.
Honourable Mr. Maya Prasad Sharma (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):-
(13:31 hours)
(..Audio missing.) There was uncertainty about whether the National Assembly meeting would convene or not, and fear, terror, and mistrust were arising. At that time, the government, through continuous discussions with citizens, discussions with parties, discussions among committees, and with all the staff, has moved forward and the 19th session has begun. For this, I want to give my heartfelt thanks to the Honourable Chairperson for the initiative. To all who cooperated. The message is being conveyed that the National Assembly exists, is alive, and is functioning. I want to thank the government very much for working hard to move this forward positively. We have all interpreted, analyzed, and discussed the movements of the 23rd and 24th. We have our own experiences of the 23rd; at that time, I had the opportunity to speak in the house. On the 23rd of Bhadra, I came in the morning. Seeing the procession coming from this side, I was heading towards the Parliament building. The Secretary-General and other staff were there, and among the parliamentarians, only I was there. Many things seemed to be in disarray, and there was a bit of fear, terror, and apprehension. Perhaps if it had been like the 24th, we would have been branded as murderers, immoral, looters, or representatives of old parties. What happened to the Secretary-General, the Secretaries, and others? It seems to have been an almost unimaginable situation and event. But what happened is that we have fortunately got the opportunity to speak in the house again. Looking at the situation where we are speaking, bringing profit to every event in life, I have also had the experience of getting an opportunity to understand it in a different way.
Honourable Chairperson, Sir, now, for our National Assembly, is there a National Assembly or not? When the parliament was dissolved, the situation was such that it was said the parliament itself was dissolved. Even the government seemed to have that feeling. In such a situation, after discussions in the committee, especially after discussions, we went north and south, and with the logic of the committee, our National Assembly was present. Asking us, "Is there a parliament? Are you still eating?" Some even said, "Are you still looting?" Such expressions were seen. But when we went there to talk about the National Assembly, we had an opportunity to discuss, and a new situation seems to have been created. Now, with the government, in our committee, in various thematic committees, in government assurances, public policy, and delegated legislation, we have called the government and discussed. Although it felt a bit awkward at times, going there and discussing happily has created a situation where the environment is becoming easier and simpler. And here, the government has just taken an initiative, the election of the National Assembly has been completed. The government has taken positively what was outside the league. The National Assembly meeting has been completed. The time for the House of Representatives election has been set, and in the election, almost all communities are going there, and parties are also becoming somewhat active. I want to take this positively. Because we have to understand the positive within the negative positively. It was not destruction, it was not damage. If our constitution had been lost today, if the President himself had been destroyed, if the country had become a playground for some foreign power, it would have been more dangerous. At least we, the people of the country, have come to a place to discuss. We have come to a place to debate in the country. We are moving forward in a process by holding elections in the country. Therefore, it is appropriate today to make this election free from rigging and impartial. Sometimes, when things go too far, is it that stunts are happening instead of thought, politics, organization, and struggle? And will this turn the country in another direction? Instead of asking what our own goal is, what is the objective, what is the vision? The wind is blowing in another direction...

In the ongoing situation, there is fear that it might lead somewhere. Prisoners have escaped, weapons are out. This will now make it a fraud. I think the government needs to think about this seriously and move towards making it free of fraud and impartial. Honorable Chairperson, yesterday when I went out of Singha Durbar, outside the room, at the south gate, a woman was lying down. The police were blocking her and telling her to go through the west gate. When asked who she was, she was a woman from Chuni Chade, Jajarkot. Specifically, Sharmila Shahi was on a hunger strike. When I went to understand what was happening, a police officer from Darcula, Bhupendra Singh Thagutra, is said to have lured her. It is said that she became pregnant, has an eight-month-old baby in her womb, and has been discussing with the government until now, but no conclusion has been reached. This needs to be resolved. We should not be looking at such ugly scenes. We need to correct this and make it stronger. On another note, yesterday, on Magh 10th, in Golbazar Municipality Ward No. 3 of Siraha, a 16-year-old girl was reportedly found hanging. Why did she die by hanging? An investigation needs to be done. During the post-mortem, it was found that another person, another girl, Radhika Shah, had taken the body of one person and cremated it, and when searching for another body, it turned out to be someone else. Why is this negligence happening? Hospital negligence, government negligence, negligence of the concerned bodies, whose negligence is it? An investigation needs to be done, and I want to demand that the government conduct an investigation. I feel these two are heading towards a dangerous situation. It has caused distress to the relatives. One person's body has been cremated, another body has been found there. Why is this happening? Therefore, I think we need to resolve this. Now, regarding the National Assembly, this government, especially the movement, the change of government, and the elections. The government has changed due to two or three movements. The main objective of the government is elections. How did this government come about? Sometimes, when a child is born illegally, the child is not at fault. It does good deeds, and its fault should not be blamed on others. How did this come about? I don't want to say anything else, but the child born illegally is not at fault. However, the parents' fault is borne by the child, and the parents, who were created by the youth movement, are like parents, and the government is like children. In terms of age, children are a bit volatile, but still, they have to take more responsibility. Those in government are a bit young. We have come through sacrifice, penance, and struggle. They spoke old words, finished them, destroyed them. We will do new things. As soon as they come, even in two months, passion arises. Those in government, saying 'now we will go to elections,' have left the government and business and gone towards elections. This is not very responsible. It is affecting others. It's not that they want to do good. They want to bring it to a conclusion. But when sitting together, its effect is sometimes felt. Therefore, I think it needs to be considered a little. The government has stopped this budget in the name of doing new things. Everyone needs development, but work has stopped there. There are national pride projects that are ongoing. These budgets have been stopped. Why was this done? This is not new; this is old. Even the Panchayat and Rana rule did nothing. This government should not be doing this. It is doing such things. It has said it will do so many things, stopping these services. What about the MPs? There is nothing. One person used to write, read, and give things, and even that has been taken away. I thought it would be done with great fear. Whether it was needed for oneself or not is another matter. But disrespecting the MPs, the legislature, the executive, and the judiciary are complementary to each other. These three are different. But if one disrespects another, things will not go well. This is our term tomorrow or the day after. We have come without any personal interests, come through the movement, fought for a lifetime, haven't we? We can be born in the mountains, we can be born on the plains, not that much, but if we change our system, if we don't follow the system, questions arise about what we are trying to do. There is a bridge in Jajarkot and Rukum, part of the Mid-Hills Highway, which has been under construction for so many years. When I was in the Constituent Assembly, it was probably Falgun month. At that time, there were three MPs from Jajarkot: Bhakta Bahadur, Kali Bahadur, and myself. We submitted it to the previous government. We gave it for the Mid-Hills. It hasn't been built yet. We have gone there; they say it's done. Today they tender, tomorrow they tender, they say. This is the situation. I think it should be done quickly. On another note, I want to say that the government should not do anything partisan. It is a coalition government; it should do coalition work. If it uplifts the nation, it will be remembered for it. Let it focus on how to make it more effective and better today, and if all parties understand the current situation positively and we hold elections, everything will fall into place. The nation will run well, and it can be run. We are not all irresponsible; we are responsible. Political party people, who does what, what do they do for a living, what do they do, we all know their history. 'The forest saw the tiger, the tiger saw the forest.' We are here. But we need to be more responsible today and uplift this country in a new way. We have brought this country through blood, tears, and sweat. Republic, federalism, secularism, as we have brought them, we need to think seriously about taking them forward. With this, I conclude my remarks. Thank you. Honorable Member Narayan Dutt Bhatta. Time: 12 minutes. (13:43) Chairperson: After this, Honorable Member Sumitra BC. Honorable Shri Narayan Dutt Bhatta (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, (13:44) Respected Honorable Members, today is also Co-existence Day. Our constitution is fragmented, and we are talking about elections. On one hand, human life lives on hope and trust; on the other hand, looking at the reality, it appears different. All the respected Honorable Members have raised the same issue: the movement of the 23rd. Everyone is saying that the demands of the movement were justified. I also want to support that. But what happened on the 24th, I think, has never happened in the world. In the days that followed, all these things, the situation, the events, the distortions, the corruption, the enmity seen in society were supposed to be overcome and move forward, but that is not the situation today. Why do I want to say this? A citizen government was formed, headed by a former judge of the respected Supreme Court. The government was formed in three or four rounds. And it was said that this is a citizen government. It has subject matter experts. It will improve the chaotic situation in the country and move forward to hold elections. I humbly request, Honorable Prime Minister Sushila Auntie, whether she formed a government of citizen leaders or not, I don't know. Bells have been rung around. I want to question those who consider themselves heroes of today's society and ask them about morality, and I want to warn those who run away from responsibility and curse the old parties. Honorable Chairperson, whether it is the words of former Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Dai, Honorable Prachanda, KP Sharma Oli, Jhalanathji, Madhav Nepal. Today, the authority you are exercising to bring about democracy is being exercised under this constitution. By cursing this authority, an attempt is being made to create a narrative that these are nothing. I want to tell them once: understand. Today, the system, the law, the process, the method in this country are all destroyed. Honorable Chairperson, I am not saying this for nothing. Media houses, which are the fourth pillar of the public, are doing journalism in the name of journalism. In the name of social media, people are being abused. I want to request, all the respected Honorable Members sitting here for the freedom to express their views, have come prepared to sacrifice their lives. But a narrative is being built: they are corrupt, they are incompetent, they are useless. I want to ask, those in positions of responsibility, who do not fulfill their responsibilities properly, are acting as stand-ups. The decision of a crowd on the 24th turned this country to ashes. What guarantee is there that those who turn this country to ashes by making the Prime Minister announcement based on the crowd today, claiming they will change the face of this country, have used the constitution to turn this country to ashes? What guarantees that they will change the face of this country? This is not symbolic. Leaving one responsibility and going to another, presenting oneself as the biggest journalist of a media house and becoming a minister, and going to the field to become a member of parliament. While people like us, bound by ideology, who work day and night for ideology and for the people, are being defamed in the name of the old. I want to tell them, perhaps the old parents were also there. The property earned by parents might also be old. Everything today might be old. Throw all that away and show that you can earn and stand on your own feet. Standing on the constitution made by others, on the blood shed by others, you are now giving sermons to everyone. I want to request, listen, this nation, nationality is not anyone's ancestral property. It is ours. But it is necessary to think. Will this nation exist or not? Where are we going? The things that are as clear as the sun here, what was in the movement of the 23rd and 24th, are always being discussed. Therefore, I want to humbly request this government. Yes, the previous government could not work; it was not in the interest of the people, and the upcoming elections will bring a government that is in the interest of the people. If there was a problem, how appropriate is it for this nation, this country, and this people to hold elections without resolving the problem? I want to ask. Just like 'Riti Ghumi Rumjhatar,' yesterday there were 4 parties, 7 parties. Now there will be only 16, 17 parties. What change will happen? What is the change they want to bring? What are the demands of the Gen Z movement? And as the accusation that we are just revolving around power continues, it's fine. Up to that point, it's fine.

What will the people coming in the upcoming elections do, will they go to Kharaani, to Gaya and Haridwar? Or are they doing politics for power? If the ultimate goal of politics is power itself, then what is the guarantee that the government that comes now will be a stable government, unlike the situation of governments changing every two or three months, which has made the people weary? Therefore, I have a request to the honorable Prime Minister and the ministers. You cannot stop a spring by blocking it; if a blocked spring bursts one day, it brings destruction. Therefore, you are blocking the spring by holding this election today. What is the way out? If we have concluded that this situation has arisen because a single party cannot get a majority in the electoral system, then the way out is to hold elections again. The movement of the 23rd and 24th has made this country a land of ashes, this country is on the grey list, by spending billions of rupees in elections, are we trying to get ourselves blacklisted and become insolvent? This is my question. Therefore, honorable Chairperson, if one path is wrong, and we take another path, thinking that it will reduce the distance by one kilometer, are we not coming back to the same place after taking a detour of five kilometers? There is a need to think about this. Elections are the backbone of democracy. The people have the right to elect representatives of their choice and to boycott those they do not want through their vote. But where will this right lead? What is the way out? Therefore, today, the constitutional bodies of the country are unable to speak, the courts are unable to speak, and it is because of us, the members of this National Assembly, that we are raising some issues here. However, the tendency to disregard and belittle this is increasing. May this government be true, move forward, and move forward in the interest of this country and its people. I welcome all the National Assembly members who will be elected in the elections. I bid farewell to all the honorable members who have given their long experience in this assembly and will be leaving after some time, expressing my respect from my side. Thank you. Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Sumitra BC. Time 14 minutes. After this (1:56 PM) Honorable Member Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar. (1:57 PM) Honorable Ms. Sumitra BC (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable Chairperson, I express my heartfelt condolences on the demise of our committee member Honorable Baldev Bohara and extend my heartfelt sympathy to the bereaved family. And I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes for a successful term to the 18 honorable members who came through the National Assembly elections on the 11th of Magh. And Chairperson, we are all victims of the current situation. And the movement or incident of the 23rd and 24th of Bhadra 2082, I believe it should be viewed from two perspectives. The voice raised by the youth for good governance and against corruption, the voice that we have all been raising, that we have been speaking in the house in the past, and that all the people wanted. The movement that raised these voices was supposed to be peaceful, and I think that taking advantage of that movement, if infiltration did not happen, then after breaking the prohibition order amidst the movement, that day, as it was the house of our National Assembly, I also came a little forward and exited from the south gate, and there, stones were thrown and fists were punched. And when the police released tear gas from there, we could not escape and there was a sister of our security guard in civilian dress. Along with her, we turned back and went to the rear. And if I think there was no infiltration, the police rules are first water cannons, then tear gas, then lathi charge, then firing in the air, then rubber bullets, and if the situation is not normal, then shooting below the knee, which was the rule of police security. Instead of that rule, due to infiltration in between, the bullets were aimed at the heads and chests of schoolchildren who came with bags and uniforms. I think those bullets were fired to incite the infiltration movement itself. I express my heartfelt tribute to the children who lost their lives. I extend my heartfelt sympathy and solidarity to the parents who were forced to bear this unbearable pain. And as a mother, I have immense sympathy for the blood shed by these children, and I find it difficult even to recall this heartbreaking incident. And as a people's representative, I want to state here that I will personally take responsibility for this. The way that incident was carried out, with the Nepali flag draped over it, damaging Nepal's pride, the way that movement was carried out, not only did it set fire to buildings the next day, but it set fire to our nationality. It set fire to our pride, and even while watching the movement with the Nepali flag, the Nepali flag was misused, and we are seeing that the Nepali flag is being misused in the elections as well. I want the current government to think seriously about this. And the incidents that happened across the country at the same time and in the same way, I think it was not just a plan for that day. This incident happened according to preparation and prior planning, and personal ancestral property of people was also burnt down, and major institutions of Nepal, the Parliament building, buildings like Singha Durbar, the backbone of the nation, and courts, presidential buildings, seeing them burnt down tears our hearts apart. And in this regard, I raised the issue in Zero Hour yesterday as well. Regarding the vehicles burnt during this time, we cannot make museums of all the buildings, but I want to reiterate today the idea of creating a museum of those burnt and smoke-damaged vehicles. And to bring the truth of that incident to light, the commission that has been formed by this government has been postponing its time. My opinion is that it should conduct a fair investigation by bringing the truth to light in time and take action against whoever is guilty. And we understand that the limit of anarchy has also been reached. And the current government, which claims to stop corruption and control anarchy, its ministers have already left their posts to become honorable members, as we all know. And this government, which came with the commitment to hold elections in these 6 months, its ministers have left their responsibilities midway. And tomorrow, regarding such tendencies, if such people are elected, what good governance can we expect? It has been almost 5 months since the government was formed. We understand that the ministers of the government have not yet submitted their asset details, which they are supposed to submit. Therefore, to criticize others, one must be capable, strong, disciplined, and ethical, and pointing fingers at others will not solve the problem. My understanding is that one must be practical. And the issue has been raised here, murder and violence are increasing. Recently, a couple was murdered in Khotang, and again, news of a mother and daughter being murdered after entering their homes is coming. And efforts are being made to cover up these murders by exchanging bodies, claiming that suspicious incidents have come to light. And regarding violence against women, even when the daughter of Jajarkot, who sat on a dharna at Maiti Ghar for almost two months, has reached the gate of Singha Durbar, there is a situation where she has not received justice. We are hearing about women who have been raped by security personnel who are supposed to protect the country and its people, and have become pregnant. For this too, I demand that the concerned bodies, the concerned Home Ministry, pay attention in time to the voice of that daughter for justice, so that the victim gets justice and the perpetrator is punished. And although the purpose of the people's movement was good, it took a terrible form. And in that context, when the House of Representatives was in session, the people felt that the National Assembly was also useless. And at least for the information of the people, it was necessary to conduct the session of this house, which is one of the two houses of this federal parliament, the National Assembly, which is an un-dissolvable house and a permanent house. It was also necessary to inform that at the national and international level, the constitution of Nepal has been somewhat torn, but not all of it has died. And in this context, all of us raised our voices, and our honorable Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, Secretariat, and the former Speaker all raised their voices and lobbied the current Prime Minister to convene this house. The President convened this house, and today we have been able to inform that we have a forum, albeit small, to raise the issues of the people and review the past, however minor. And the Nepali people will be aware of those who are creating this kind of anarchy, and in the upcoming elections, instead of individuals who are doing such stunts without principles or organization, the people will vote thoughtfully to protect this system, which has been achieved through the sacrifice of many martyrs who have moved forward in an organized manner and contributed, and to keep this constitution alive and continue it, to oppose the shortcomings and tendencies here, to correct them, to maintain the good things and move forward, to develop the country, and to amend necessary laws, representatives of the people are needed again. And I sincerely request that the Nepali people will vote thoughtfully in this election to correct the tendencies of their leaders and protect this system. And the problems piled up here, we will address those problems with a common approach. (Time ended.) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar. Time 12 minutes. (2:11 PM) After this, Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota. Honorable Mr. Bhuvan Bahadur Sunar (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Center):- (2:11 PM) Honorable Chairperson, the 19th session of the National Assembly has begun. This is a matter of great happiness for us. It is a matter of great happiness for the Nepali people. Why? Because yesterday there was a rumor that the parliament was dissolved. And this is ours... it was said to be not... but in the understanding of the general public, there is no parliament in Nepal now. The understanding that existed, and this understanding, due to the efforts of the honorable Chairperson, the Secretariat, and the positive understanding of the current government, the National Assembly has begun. With its beginning, the message is going out nationally and internationally that there is a National Assembly in Nepal, not all parliaments have been dissolved. This is a matter of happiness. Why? Because it has greatly dispelled the understanding that all institutions that give voice to the people have been destroyed. And now, when the institution that gives voice to the people is alive, and our issues are raised here, and our issues are heard and attract the attention of the state, our role will remain with that understanding. But the tragedy is that the country is going towards ruin day by day. Because this new activity will solve the problems of the country and open a good path.

It was there, but looking at it now, it is going more towards crisis, more towards corruption. Questions have been raised. What happened then? The three pillars of state governance are the executive, the legislature, and the judiciary. If these institutions function properly, then good governance will prevail, and the country will move forward. However, the legislature can form and dissolve the executive, can hold it accountable, and can prevent arbitrariness. Similarly, the legislature will not allow the executive to be arbitrary. Likewise, even though the judiciary is independent, the legislature can conduct hearings and impeach it. These are our constitutional provisions. But when instead of good governance, misgovernance prevails, corruption and irregularities flourish, the judiciary tries to run the government, issues various orders and obstructs work, the government tries to make the parliament a rubber stamp, tries to control it, these are the current situations. The government cannot cut the plans passed by the parliament as it pleases. The plans made by the parliament, the plans and programs allocated by the parliament, the government is arbitrarily stopping and cutting them. What happens because of this kind of activity? The government seeks to be arbitrary. The government should not have done such a big job. This government should have established good governance in the country and completed the elections. We think the government is going on a path, elections will be held, the question of whether elections will be held or not will not arise. Why? Because elections are only about a month away. People are still creating hype, saying elections will not happen, parliament will be reinstated. This statement is not really a correct statement, it has not come from the right place. In such a situation, the government should abide by the issues raised in the parliament and the directives given by the parliament and its committees. This is not being followed. And it is not known where the government's policies, methods, and decisions are being run from. There is a discussion outside that the government is run by smugglers, by middlemen, or that it is being run from outside. Such suspicions are arising. Let me give an example of what design and what setting this is happening in. Things are happening strangely, like the cases of GB, Ravi, and Chhobi. What is being attempted by amending the charge sheets of these cases and the charge sheets of about 50 people, such as cases of cooperatives, money laundering, and organized crime? There is doubt among people. Is it that all these cases are being withdrawn? Is the government trying to give amnesty? Such doubts have arisen in people's minds. Such discussions are taking place. Why is this happening? Why were they imprisoned yesterday? What happened again? What happened that they were released again? These activities have not sent a good message. In our village, they say, "No matter who the monk is, his ears are pierced." I used to wonder what this meant. Now, the state of this government appears to be like that. This government was supposed to end good governance, corruption, and irregularities. It moved forward with such a grand slogan, but the situation has arisen where this is not the case. Now, how will the government defend itself? It must defend itself by becoming an example. The issues being discussed the most, the things that have happened here, the issue of companies like Dolma has been raised. For example, the government decides to give huge tax exemptions, to take all profits abroad or to Mauritius without paying capital gains tax, causing a revenue deficit. Why is this being done against the spirit of the constitution and the law? Why is this happening? What is the reason for this? And why are the bodies that do this, the institutions and individuals that cover up the truth in the place of justice, why do they have such wrong intentions? These intentions need to be investigated, and action must be taken against the places, institutions, and individuals who have such intentions. This is the government's responsibility. But we hear and see the government remaining silent on this issue, and nothing significant is seen. Is this all? We have also heard other things, and there is much discussion now. Why is the government not taking action? Why is the government silent? For example, whether to protect the gangs involved in smuggling girls' eggs or to investigate and take action against them. The government's role is not visible in this matter either. Will the government do good work in a short time and then come back to power, or will this government become more infamous and say that the previous government did not do good work? The new government should have done good work. Has this government also done the same, or even worse than that situation? It is not right to become so infamous in such a short time. In such a situation, the government should function according to the people's will and sentiment. Work should be done. The expectations that the people have are not being met. We hope that this government will work according to those expectations, and in the coming days, when the new government comes after the elections, it will reward this government and congratulate it. With this, I conclude my short speech. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota. Time: 11 minutes. (2:22 PM) After this, Honorable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari. Honorable Shree Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, (2:23 PM) The 18th session concluded in an unimaginable situation. Witnessing firsthand the future torchbearers of the country, the youth, falling, the parliament building itself burning, and finding myself speechless, that pain still burns my heart and makes me cry today. In Nepal, the birthplace of Lord Buddha, the pioneer of peace, such acts have bowed the heads of Nepal and Nepalis. Nevertheless, after a long interval, connecting broken hearts, repairing burnt physical structures, the 19th session of the Federal Parliament, the National Assembly, which speaks and listens to the voices of the citizens, has been successful in starting, so we have been able to speak our suppressed voices. Congratulations and best wishes to all of us for this. Honorable Chairperson, in the meantime, we have lost Honorable late Baldev Bohora, who emerged as a democratic warrior from Sudurpashchim, a member of the National Assembly. I offer my heartfelt tribute to him. Similarly, against the rampant corruption, unemployment, and weak governance growing in the country, and the social media, which has been disseminating information worldwide, being suddenly shut down, leading to anger and pain from villages to cities, the youth's rebellion exploded onto the streets. Taking advantage of the movement, some people fished in troubled waters. I express my heartfelt condolences and eternal peace to those innocent young brothers and sisters who were martyred while presenting their voices in school and college uniforms. I extend my heartfelt sympathy to the bereaved families who have lost their children. I wish a speedy recovery to the injured brothers and sisters. Honorable Chairperson, the demands of the youth on Bhadra 23rd were indeed just. What was wrong with them demanding freedom from corruption, arranging employment for youth migrating abroad within the country, making citizens' daily services simple and easy instead of cumbersome, establishing good governance, and properly utilizing and expanding new technologies through peaceful protests? They were only holding accountable some top leaders who have been in power for a long time. No one said that anyone's house, any leader's house should be burnt, or any leader should be beaten. They did not say to implement what is written in the constitution, to dissolve and restructure the parliament. They said to make the legislature, executive, and judiciary efficient, effective, and organized, and not to discriminate. They did not say to burn down historical buildings with documents, but why and how did this happen? These things are still questionable today. Honorable Chairperson, where is the country heading today? Who is running this country? Who is running it from where? What is our country's CIB watching? Is the peace and security of our country helpless, has it become helpless? Where was the Nepali Army? When the President's Shital Niwas was burning fiercely, why did the army just watch? Why couldn't they stop the innocent youth in school and college uniforms from being killed by indiscriminate firing in front of them? Why couldn't they extinguish the fire burning in the courtyard of their own home? Why couldn't they stop the masked individuals from easily entering Singha Durbar from the gate? Or is it the misfortune of this country that our government is still ignorant? Today, is the world-famous bravery of the brave Gorkhalis truly mute and helpless? The problems are complex, yet the government is silent. Honorable Chairperson, I say that the movement on Bhadra 23rd was with the just demands of the youth and was natural. But the extreme cowardice and treason of the vandals on Bhadra 24th was treasonous. To bring the country out of its critical situation and to extinguish the fire that was raging like a storm, the Honorable President played a role by risking his life and limb, trying to save the constitution made by the citizens, even if it was an unconstitutional decision. Just as in 2033 BS, Mahamanav BP Koirala, setting aside the treason and murder charges against him, dedicated himself to the nation and said that his throat and the King's throat were the same on the issue of nationality, risking his life. Honorable Chairperson, some ministers of the government formed in the name of the feelings and respect of the youth, suddenly proved themselves to be independent individuals and, on the pretext of being connected with the feelings of the youth, took an oath to this constitution and occupied ministerial chairs in the people's government. As soon as they occupied the ministerial seats, their attachment to the chair and power grew. Then, contrary to the feelings of the youth, their only refrain was elections. They kept repeating only elections. When the announcement of elections was made, they abandoned their responsibilities, duties, and ethics, left the government, and went to the election field carrying the flags of specific parties. Is there any place left for citizens to trust and believe? Yet, we Nepalis are quick to get angry and quick to forget today. Honorable Chairperson, the things we have been raising repeatedly in the parliament, we have been trying to alert the government. Our voices were for the creation of a corruption-free society, good governance, and an employment-oriented economy, for generating income through small and medium-sized industries and cottage industries in the country, processing local liquor, branded nettle, and many herbs like cannabis, formulating policies and regulations for them, establishing them as small and medium-sized cottage industries, and providing employment to citizens. Trade, business, service with a smile, and work with respect. But those voices were confined only to the camera's lens and the pages of documents. As a result, the physical structures built with loans, aid, and assistance from other countries worldwide have turned to ashes. There has been a huge loss of life and property. After all, the demands of the youth were nothing more than this. Honorable Chairperson, ordinary people...

And by not paying attention to small things, the country has faced a disaster today. Even though we are heading into elections today, the citizens are not able to be happy. On one hand, escaped prisoners are returning to jail, and on the other hand, looted weapons have not all been recovered. Street crimes are increasing day by day. Theft, robbery, rape, fraud (...time expired).
Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari. Time 12 minutes. (14:34 PM)
Honorable Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepal Communist Party (Maoist Centre)): Honorable Chairperson, I would like to extend my best wishes for the success of the 19th session of the National Assembly. Similarly, I would like to offer my heartfelt condolences to Honorable Baldev Bohara, a member of the National Assembly and also a member of the Public Policy and Proportional Legislation Committee.
Honorable Chairperson, the country is currently heading into mid-term elections in the special circumstances arising from the events of Bhadra 23 and 24. We are all aware of the factors that led to this situation. We have made a constitution. In the constitution, we have ensured the economic, social, cultural rights, and political rights of all classes, oppressed, ethnic groups, linguistic groups, regional groups, gender groups, marginalized, and minority oppressed communities, and institutionalized these rights as fundamental rights. We have managed education, health, employment, food, shelter, and housing rights as fundamental rights. Without the full implementation of the fundamental rights guaranteed by the constitution, the people cannot feel that their situation has changed. To some extent, political rights were ensured, but the people's lives did not change economically, and the people began to feel that. There was a commitment to enact all laws within three years of the constitution's promulgation. The people have also taken into account the reality that we could not enact laws on time. More than 200 laws, including the Federal Education Act, Federal Police Adjustment Act, and Federal Employee Act, related to directive principles and fundamental rights, are still pending. When we talk about good governance, we have hung "zero tolerance for corruption" on the wall. But it did not happen in practice. The people could not experience zero tolerance in practice. Similarly, in this process, incidents like the Baluwatar, Bansbari, Tribhuvan University land grab cases, fake Bhutanese refugees, and Yeti Omni case have increased the level of despair and anger among the people. Since the formation of the 18-month government under the leadership of Comrade Prachanda, work to establish good governance, integrity, and fulfill the needs of the people's livelihood has progressed in a more constructive manner. The Nepali people have also seen this reality. In accordance with the policy of not sparing the guilty and not harming the innocent, dozens of ministers, employees, and officers who reached high positions were brought under investigation. Hundreds of corruption files were opened, which brought a ray of hope and expectation among the general public for the establishment of good governance. The people also deeply observed and felt the fact that the Prachanda-led government collapsed overnight due to the fear that the investigation would reach the highest levels of political parties, starting with the arrest of Bechan Jha.
Honorable Chairperson, before the movement, the coalition government of the CPN UML led by leader K.P. Sharma Oli and the Congress, formed with a certain process and commitment. The activities of the government, which aimed to provide stability to the country, establish good governance, achieve zero tolerance for corruption, fulfill all the needs of the people, and provide stability, led to further anger among the people and turned the hope that had recently emerged into complete despair. As an expression of that, when social media was banned. The only place for young people to speak on social media was expressing dissatisfaction with various issues, including the increasing exodus of youth. When social media was shut down, on the 23rd, the youth raised three issues. Specifically, in favor of good governance, in favor of lifting the ban on social media, and for stability, this debate should begin to move the country towards the executive once. This was the main sentiment of the youth on the 23rd. The sentiment, demands, and issues of the youth movement on the 23rd were neither anti-constitution, nor anti-system, nor based on the idea of bringing the country into disaster. It was a correct expectation, but the government did not look at it deeply, did not introspect. The government did not feel what was brewing inside, the then government. And 23 innocent, unarmed students were killed. Penetration, infiltration, etc., were not in the government's information at once. The government was unaware of how the movement would break out, and a situation arose where commandos had to be used. Commandos do not shoot below the knee; commandos shoot at the chest. We also saw that incident inside the parliament building that day.
And when an atmosphere of general public outrage was created for the 24th, elements with various vested interests, both domestic and foreign, who wanted to destabilize and create anarchy in this country, to make this country fail, and to fulfill their own interests, infiltrated the movement on the 24th, burning all structures of the executive, judiciary, and legislature to make the state completely fail, and causing great damage to national property. Not only that, but offices of political parties, commercial buildings, and even the houses of political leaders were burned. This is unfortunate, and it is the general understanding today that if the then Prime Minister and Home Minister had resigned on the evening of the 23rd, understanding the psychology of the 23rd, the incident of the 24th would not have occurred. And the issues raised by the new youth on Bhadra 23rd, after the destructive events of the 24th, the first priority was to save the constitution in the situation that arose in the country. The role played by the Honorable President to save the constitution, and the role played by leaders like Pushpa Kamal Dahal "Prachanda" and Madhav Nepal of the Nepali Communist Party, among others, is commendable. And today, to save the constitution, which is on the brink, the government, the government formed after this, whose responsibility was to conduct elections, I thank this government in this sense because this government is committed to conducting elections, and the atmosphere for elections has been building up so far. And I also want to draw the government's attention to this: this current government has also not become the government according to the expectations of the youth movement. Neither the youth have reached the leadership of the government, nor the youth. Nor have the corruption files that were investigated in the past, which the previous K.P. Oli-led government had closed. Now, this government is also working in a way that some of these corrupt individuals will get immunity. Again, I do not want to comment much on the government because its main responsibility is to conduct elections and it is committed to elections.
Honorable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention. Everyone is interested in this election. It is the government's responsibility to conduct the election. It is the responsibility of the parties to create an environment for the election. Today, there is a national atmosphere, and there is national and international interest in this election. In this regard, I want to say that the government should move forward with good preparations to conduct this election peacefully, impartially, without rigging, and without fear. And at the same time, I want to appeal to the Nepali people from this rostrum: do not vote for those who have sacrificed any agenda, slogan, or originality. You have sacrificed to bring this system, to change this situation, to change the current situation, to change the system, to play a role in changing the current situation, to protect the constitution, to strengthen democracy, to bring social justice, prosperity, development, and to end corruption, and to take this country towards socialism. Be aware of the tendencies that create chaos in this country, and I want to appeal to the honorable public to vote for the parties that will fight against all such tendencies and lead this country in the right direction. Let us not be misled, and the first thing this country needs is to protect the constitution, to enact laws on the subjects prescribed by the constitution, to provide employment to the people as soon as possible, to improve education and health, to strengthen federalism, and to strengthen the governments at all three levels. The responsibility that lies on our shoulders. The elected government that will come will fulfill that responsibility. It will address the expectations and demands of the youth. The country needs to move forward on that basis. I conclude my brief remarks by saying these things. Thank you. Greetings.
(14:47 PM)
Honorable Chairperson: The order of speaking by honorable members during special time is now concluded. Honorable members, now I would like to provide time to the Chairperson of the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee, Honorable Kamala Pant, to present the annual report of the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee for the fiscal year 2081/082 before the assembly.
Honorable Chairperson of the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee, Ms. Kamala Pant: Honorable Chairperson, as per Article 97, Sub-section (1) of the Constitution of Nepal and Rule 146 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, subject committees and special committees can be formed within the National Assembly to assist in the regular work of the National Assembly. As per Rule 147, Sub-rule (1) of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, the Development, Economic Affairs and Good Governance Committee is a permanent subject committee among the subject committees formed to monitor and evaluate the government's actions and provide necessary directives or advice to make the government accountable to the assembly. Honorable Chairperson, the committee's scope of work includes development plans, projects, sustainable development, equitable and balanced development, investment, population management, Nepal's economy, public finance, pre-budget discussions, good governance and administrative reform, information technology, and innovation, and related bodies. Taking information about the policies, programs, plans, budgets, resource mobilization, and management of all ministries, departments, and development projects under them, related to sustainable development and good governance, and making appropriate decisions also falls within the committee's scope of work. Annual work plans have been prepared according to the committee's scope of work, and the committee's activities have been conducted. The committee's annual report for 2081/082 has been prepared, covering the activities carried out by the committee from July 1, 2081, to June 30, 2082.
Honorable Chairperson, good governance is essential for strengthening democratic governance, and social justice and prosperity can be achieved through the promotion of good governance. Therefore, the committee appears to be active in establishing good governance in the political, administrative, judicial, private, and non-governmental sectors. The committee has always been active and ready to make all the development activities of the government sustainable, balanced, and inclusive. To achieve the expected results of the Sustainable Development Goals, which are currently a global agenda, within the stipulated time, the committee has been providing necessary directives and coordination...

The government has been monitoring all government activities to promote good governance. The Sustainable Development Goals have been integrated into all development activities, all provinces, and local levels by updating indicators of Sustainable Development Goals in the provinces and coding SDG in the national budget. Interactive sessions at the provincial level on Sustainable Development Goals have been implemented to make the process responsible and effective. The committee has continuously studied, monitored, discussed, and overseen the implementation of the recommendations made in the "Study and Evaluation Report on the Status of Sustainable Development Goal Implementation in Nepal, 2080".

Honorable Chairperson, the Ministry of Finance has been directed to include issues of good governance, social justice, sustainable development, and prosperity in the budget by specifying the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill, 2082, and pre-budget discussions. The committee, after discussing the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill, 2082, presented to the House, with the National Planning Commission, the Ministry of Finance, scholars from various sectors, stakeholders, concerned bodies, non-governmental sectors, private and cooperative sectors, has made recommendations to the government for budget formulation. It seems necessary to provide time for the government to present the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill to the House for discussion and to implement the recommendations made by the committee and to make pre-budget discussions effective. Honorable Chairperson, I would like to submit that the government has only been listening to the directives given by the parliament and the committee during pre-budget discussions and budget allocation.

The committee has been directing and monitoring the ministries to include programs in the budget according to the 16th plan, to accelerate development construction activities based on priority by classifying projects, to make road infrastructure and transportation management safe and organized, to develop disaster-resilient infrastructure, and to complete projects on time by mobilizing human resources and making necessary preparations to increase capital expenditure. The progress of the ministry's capital budget has been discussed and monitored for the effective implementation of the development budget.

26

Honorable Chairperson, the committee has been continuously working to mainstream women, Dalits, persons with disabilities, minority communities, and all citizens into development. The committee regulates the government's activities by regularly monitoring and studying the implementation of the policy proposals passed by the National Assembly and provides necessary directives. It is deemed necessary to emphasize the implementation of the "Report on the Need for Legal Arrangements Regarding the Rights and Development of the Dalit Community, 2081" as specified in Article 40 of the Constitution of Nepal. The committee has been effectively conducting its work by forming sub-committees for Sustainable Development, Economic Affairs, Good Governance Promotion, and Policy Proposal Implementation Monitoring, and through them, conducting in-depth and extensive studies and investigations on specified areas, and discussing them in the committee. The "Study Report on Nepal's Graduation from Least Developed Country to Developing Country, 2081" prepared by the committee and presented to the House has been directed by the House to the Government of Nepal for implementation of the recommendations mentioned therein. The government's attention has been drawn to continuously monitor Nepal's participation in the annual global climate conferences to make it productive, provide necessary directives, and prepare future work plans by reviewing after the conference. It is a matter of regret, Honorable Chairperson, that the committee cannot present those issues. The government does not know, does not participate in the conference, and does not know its own affairs. The government's activities regarding the easy management of chemical fertilizers for farmers, making agricultural subsidies production-oriented, managing the production and market of agricultural products, and conserving and developing indigenous agricultural crops have been monitored. The committee has played a leading role in making climate change-targeted actions effective, drawing the government's attention to the acquisition and utilization of climate finance, continuously monitoring good governance promotion, and drawing the attention of stakeholders to disaster management.

Strengthening

Honorable Chairperson, it is imperative to draw the government's attention to issuing a National Integrity Policy to strengthen democratic governance and promote good governance. The National Assembly and its committees must play a responsible role in increasing mutual relations, cooperation, and coordination among federal units to strengthen federalism, and in formulating policies and laws on the concurrent rights of all three tiers mentioned in the constitution.

27

The committee's scope of work is extensive and broad, which has prevented it from focusing on specific tasks. The committee's term of two years and the frequent rotation of honorable members also hinder the committee's work. Problems such as a lack of physical, technical, and financial resources to make the committee's work effective, the government's lack of activeness in accountability for implementing the committee's directives, and the absence of legal policies and structural mechanisms to make the implementation of directives mandatory have been realized. Finally, I express my sincere gratitude to the Honorable Chairperson and the Honorable Vice-Chairperson for their continuous guidance to the committee's work. I also extend my thanks and gratitude to the honorable members who have diligently worked for the committee, the honorable ministers, honorable members of the National Assembly, honorable members of the House of Representatives, the Secretary-General of the Federal Parliament, the Secretary of the National Assembly, the committee's secretary, government employees, subject matter experts, secretariat staff, security personnel, and journalists, and all stakeholders who have supported our work directly and indirectly by being present in the meetings. Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, in accordance with the decision of the committee's meeting held on Jestha 5, 2082, I present the Annual Report of the Committee, 2081/082, to the respected House as per Rule 159 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, now I would like to provide time to the Honorable Chairperson of the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee, Maya Prasad Sharma, to present the Annual Report of the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee for the fiscal year 2081/082 to the House.

(14:59 hrs)

Honorable Chairperson of the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee, Mr. Maya Prasad Sharma:- Honorable Chairperson, the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee of the National Assembly decided on its meeting held on Magh 8, 2082, to pass its Sixth Annual Report, 2081/082, and present it to the House. This report has been prepared based on the work, discussions, interactive programs, field observations, and committee decisions made by the committee from Shrawan 1, 2081, to Asar end, 2082, as well as other activities.

(15:00 hrs)

Honorable Chairperson, first of all, the committee mourns the untimely demise of Honorable Baldev Bohara, a member of the National Assembly and the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee, on Poush 30, 2082. On behalf of the committee, I offer my heartfelt condolences to the departed honorable member and express deep sympathy to the bereaved family.

Honorable Chairperson, the Public Policy and Delegated Legislation Committee was formed in accordance with Rule 147 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, to support the regular functioning of the National Assembly, to make the Government of Nepal accountable and responsible to the National Assembly, to evaluate and study the public policies of the Government of Nepal, to study delegated legislation, to provide necessary directives and suggestions to the government by studying and observing historical and archaeological heritage and national important documents, and to monitor and evaluate the actions taken by the Government of Nepal and provide necessary directives or advice. The committee has been given the responsibility of discussing and providing suggestions on the draft stage of the sectoral policies of the Government of Nepal, and analyzing, monitoring, and evaluating the sectoral policies that have been issued and providing directives. Similarly, the responsibility of parliamentary oversight has been assigned to this committee to examine whether the subordinate legislation formulated by the Government of Nepal using delegated authority is inconsistent with the objective, spirit, and intent of the parent law, whether it conforms to the principles of natural justice, whether it grants excessive discretionary power through subordinate law, and whether the subordinate laws are made contrary to the spirit of the Constitution of Nepal and the parent act.

To make the government accountable to the parliament, to make the government's actions transparent in the country, to promote good governance, and to ensure good governance, the committee's scope of work includes studying and monitoring whether the written and oral assurances given regarding the implementation of government programs, budgets, question-and-answer sessions, bill discussions, attention-grabbing motions, and policy proposals presented by the government to the federal parliament have been fulfilled, and to identify shortcomings and provide suggestions and directives to the Government of Nepal and concerned bodies for improvement in the areas of studying and monitoring historical and archaeological heritage and national important documents and records management.

Honorable Chairperson, during the reporting period, the committee held 67 full meetings, and the sub-committees formed under the committee held a total of 58 meetings. Reports related to the damage, rehabilitation, and reconstruction caused by the Jajarkot earthquake, reports prepared regarding delegated legislation under the Tribhuvan University Act, and reports related to the policy issues concerning the conflict between conservation and development of national parks have been submitted to the respected House. Similarly, during this reporting period, the committee has held discussions and interactions on related issues with honorable ministers of the Government of Nepal, officials of constitutional bodies, secretaries of the Government of Nepal, heads of departments, subject matter experts, and representatives of stakeholder groups. The committee has held joint meetings with other committees as needed on matters related to its scope of work, and has also obtained necessary information by conducting field observations, monitoring, and inspections in various places within different provinces. During field observations, discussions and interactions were held with people's representatives of the concerned local levels, members of the provincial assembly of the concerned provinces, and concerned communities. Furthermore, due to the committee's initiative, the renovation work related to the old House of Representatives building (Gallery Meeting) has been decided by the respected court, and reconstruction work is currently underway. All the work done by the committee during the reporting period...

The detailed report is included in the report. I would like to extend my heartfelt thanks to the subcommittee conveners and all the honorable members and the committee secretariat for actively performing their duties during this period of the committee. I express my sincere gratitude and thanks to the honorable Chairperson and the honorable Vice-Chairperson of the National Assembly for always providing us with advice, suggestions, and guidance. I thank the honorable Prime Minister, honorable ministers, secretaries of the Government of Nepal, and other civil servants, the Secretary-General of the Federal Parliament, the Secretary of the National Assembly, all the staff, the civil servants of the security agencies, and the media personnel from all sectors of society for their continuous cooperation in the committee's work. Finally, honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the honorable Chairperson, I present the Sixth Annual Report of the Committee on Public Policy and Delegated Legislation, 2082, to the honorable assembly. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I provide time to the Honorable Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation, Anil Kumar Sinha, to present the proposal to send the Bill on Intangible Cultural Heritage Conservation, 2081, to the Legislative Management Committee for clause-by-clause discussion. Honorable Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation, Anil Kumar Sinha: Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present the proposal to send the Bill on Intangible Cultural Heritage Conservation, 2081, to the Legislative Management Committee for clause-by-clause discussion to this honorable assembly. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I now present the Bill on Intangible Cultural Heritage Conservation, 2081, to the Legislative Management Committee for decision regarding clause-by-clause discussion. Honorable members who are in favor of this proposal will say "Yes" and honorable members who are against it will say "No." Honorable members in favor of this proposal, say "Yes." - "Yes" Honorable members against this proposal, say "No." The sound of "No" was not heard. Therefore, I declare that the proposal to send the Bill on Intangible Cultural Heritage Conservation, 2081, to the Legislative Management Committee for clause-by-clause discussion has been unanimously approved. Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Monday, Magh 19, 2082, at 1:15 PM, and this meeting is hereby adjourned. (Thereafter, the next meeting was adjourned to be held on Monday, Magh 19, 2082, at 1:15 PM.) Adjournment: 03:09 PM.

sections.summary_en: Honourable Maya Prasad Sharma spoke about the successful commencement of the 19th session of the National Assembly amidst political uncertainty and thanked those involved. He also reflected on the events of Bhadra 23 and 24, emphasizing the importance of dialogue and the functioning of the National Assembly.

speakers.topic: Resumption of National Assembly and political reflections

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker expresses concerns about potential fraud in elections and highlights issues of public safety and negligence in government services. They also criticize the current government's formation and actions, questioning its legitimacy and effectiveness.

They criticize the government's actions, such as stopping budgets and disrespecting MPs, and question the legitimacy of the current political direction.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari analyzes the political situation leading to mid-term elections, highlighting unfulfilled constitutional promises regarding fundamental rights and the slow pace of lawmaking. He criticizes corruption and various scandals, contrasting them with the perceived efforts of the Prachanda-led government. He further discusses the K.P. Oli-led government's actions, the social media ban, and the subsequent youth protests on Bhadra 23rd, which he argues were a legitimate expression of public discontent. He details the events of Bhadra 23rd and 24th, including student deaths and widespread destruction, attributing them to government inaction and external elements. He praises the roles of the President and leaders like Prachanda and Madhav Nepal in saving the constitution and expresses gratitude to the current government for its commitment to holding elections, while also noting its shortcomings in addressing youth expectations and past corruption cases. He appeals to the public to vote for progressive forces that uphold the constitution, democracy, and social justice.
